hpi:
{{patient_name}} is a postpartum woman presenting with palpitations and tremor. She is breastfeeding. The symptoms began gradually after delivery and have been worsening. She denies chest pain, dyspnea, or syncope. No personal or family history of thyroid disease.

Diagnosis: Postpartum Thyroiditis — an autoimmune disorder that attacks the thyroid similar to Hashimoto's thyroiditis. Antibodies against the thyroid cause inflammation which damages thyroid follicles, causing release of large amounts of T4/T3 into circulation. Most symptomatic patients recover within 1 year. The hyperthyroidism is transitory.

Key differential: Graves' disease. In Graves', T3 is more elevated than T4. In postpartum thyroiditis, T4 is typically elevated while T3 is slightly elevated or within normal limits. Free T4 is disproportionately elevated (~4x ULN) while Free T3 is only borderline elevated — this is the classic pattern.

Workup: thyroid exam (HEENT/Neck), CBC, T3/T4/TSH, BMP. Optional: thyroid antibody, thyroid US (low blood flow = postpartum thyroiditis vs high flow = Graves).

Treatment: Propranolol for symptomatic relief (safe in breastfeeding). Avoid Atenolol (less preferred for breastfeeding), Methimazole/PTU (T4/T3 synthesis decreased, not increased, in this condition), thyroid uptake/scan (radioactive, contraindicated in breastfeeding).

Follow-up: Serial free T4/TSH. May enter hypothyroid phase requiring levothyroxine. Most stabilize within 1 year postpartum.

physical_exam: Appears anxious, fine tremor of outstretched hands. No acute distress.
Tachycardic, regular rhythm. No murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Brisk pulses.
Thyroid mildly enlarged, non-tender, no discrete nodules. No lid lag or proptosis.
Clear to auscultation. No respiratory distress.
Warm, moist. No rash. Normal capillary refill.

patient_voice.history: {{patient_name}} is a postpartum woman presenting with palpitations and tremor. She is breastfeeding. Symptoms began gradually after delivery and have been worsening. She denies chest pain, dyspnea, or syncope.
patient_voice.pain: None. Just this fluttering feeling in my chest and my hands shake.

case_summary: Postpartum Thyroiditis — autoimmune destruction of thyroid follicles releasing stored T4/T3. Disproportionately elevated T4 relative to T3 distinguishes from Graves' disease. Transitory hyperthyroidism; most recover within 1 year. Symptomatic treatment with propranolol (breastfeeding-safe). Avoid radioactive studies and thionamides.
